name: v4.3.0 - Law and Language
body:
Magelight UI 1.0.0 is bundled (`98 Magelight UI`), the first stable version. Since 0.31.2:

- Behind an ENB, ReShade or another `d3d11.dll` / `dxgi.dll` wrapper, menus no longer open invisible: they draw in the game's own interface pass without editing `Magelight.json`.
- Changing UI Scale in Settings rebuilds the menu at the new size, so the text stays sharp instead of blurring until a restart.
- Typing into a menu no longer sets off other mods' hotkeys that read the keyboard directly.
- A PC whose fallback font cannot load no longer loses every menu, and fonts in folders with non-English names load.
- VR: closing a page with a controller button no longer passes that button to the game.
- `Magelight.log` starts with what the game runs on (game, SKSE, Windows, graphics card) and writes your Windows user folder as `%USERPROFILE%`.

World > Law & Crime replaces the Arrests tab and brings bounties and arrests onto one page: your bounty in each of the nine holds (with Clear, Clear All and Add bounty, a bounty you put on yourself for roleplay), arrests under way, the jail roster beside your people who are wanted, and captives. Enterprises keeps the debts, on a tab now called Debts. Every guard, jarl, housecarl and steward of a hold knows what you are wanted for there, not just the amount. Guards can charge an NPC with a crime, the jail roster remembers what each prisoner was jailed for, a jarl or housecarl can pardon a prisoner held anywhere in their hold, and a guard freeing a prisoner unlocks the cell door. An arrest is jailed in the hold where it happens instead of falling back to Whiterun; an arrest in a hold SeverActions cannot place (Solstheim, a modded hold) is refused.

A guard who tries to arrest one of your followers, or a retainer on guard duty, talks to them first. They can pay the charge (a fine, or a bribe for a large bounty), go quietly or refuse; the guard can drop the charge, press it or take them in. The talk keeps going on its own and ends after a time limit (150 seconds by default) with a verdict. Refusing is a real fight: the guard beats them into submission and takes them in, or they get away, and if you hit the guard yourself the fight becomes yours and they rejoin you. An arrested follower stays arrested: nothing pulls them back to you, they keep their own clothes in jail, and they serve a set time (one day by default, or until you free them). The settings are in Settings > Arrest.

Settings > UI Display has a Language setting: the game's language (the default), English, French, Russian or Japanese, whatever language the game is in. Every page, popup and the quick wheel is translated into French, Russian and Japanese, and the payment, debt, trade and letter cards no longer show in English on a translated game. Messages at the top of the screen follow the setting where the game's font can draw it. Names from the game and other mods, text already saved in a save file and some notifications stay as they are.

Outfits for you: the Outfits page has a You entry. Save what you are wearing, map outfits to situations (combat, sleep, rain, snow, home, town, adventure) and your own auto-switch changes you when the situation does, or put one on with Wear Now. It only swaps your own gear: it never adds, removes or copies an item, and it never takes off something you put on yourself unless the new outfit needs the slot. A mirror shows you, and Try On dresses you in an outfit you are building, lending catalog pieces you do not own until you close the menu.

For NPCs, the auto-switch can borrow a related outfit for a situation with none mapped (Outfits > Outfit Settings > Borrow Related Outfits, off by default), puts back what they wore before a fight, and changes at doors and beds without the usual delay. With the Tailor mod installed, SeverActions leaves the NPCs Tailor dresses to it (a setting on the Outfits page). Children are never dressed or undressed. An NPC's own default outfit can be cleared and restored from their wardrobe, and outfit pieces another mod forces on them come off. Saved presets on non-followers survive a force-remove, and there are 200 outfit slots instead of 100. Taking a piece of an NPC's active preset off them leaves them one copy, so it no longer duplicates. Hair in the mirror looks as full as in game.

Bio Blocks come in two starter packs, General (113 blocks, with religion, dislikes, phobias and vices new) and Adult (67), added or removed on the Bio Blocks page. Adult tabs sit under a folded Adult heading and stay out of All blocks and searches. A tab can be set to one block per NPC, so applying a block replaces the other one from that tab. Libraries from before 3.9.13 get no duplicates: your old copies of the shipped blocks are recognised and take the cleaned wording, and nothing you wrote or edited is touched. For mod authors, the Bio Blocks API (v4) lists the blocks an NPC carries and every block in the library, announces changes, and reaches SeverActions' own blocks by key.

NPCs move money on their own again: a merchant or innkeeper bills you for what they just did (you confirm it), and a grateful NPC tips or rewards you now and then. Merchants recite their shop stock only at their shop and during opening hours, judged from the game's merchant records, so it works on a translated game and with modded merchants. A follower eats from their pack as soon as they would start complaining of hunger, Force Feed counts the food's own value, and a fed follower stops bringing up an old complaint. An NPC who writes to ask for work remembers writing the letter. Rumours are kept one list per hold, and a pinned rumour no longer reaches every NPC in Skyrim.

Outlaw camps: the camp challenge waits until someone in the camp actually spots you, so sneaking through unseen is never challenged, and sneaking near outlaws who have not seen you no longer breaks the truce. With the truce off, wild camps go quiet and camps sworn to you keep the peace; turning off necromancers or the Forsworn releases those already calmed. A vampire follower no longer reads the bandit standoff text. A deserter's grudge ambush and a captive's search party count only once they actually come, a reload gives them back, and a refused ransom stuck on a lost search reopens. Only fences serve jail terms; other retainers taken by the guards wait in jail until you bail them.

Also: on Skyrim AE a travelling follower is no longer stopped as "dead", a companion making an arrest is no longer pulled back to you through a door, the stall after loading a save is shorter on large load orders, a follower relaxing at home is released properly when you leave, and the AttackTarget error in the Papyrus log on the player is gone. The old orphan-cleanup scanner is removed, with its setting.

Installing this version: install it over 4.2.x with Replace. The installer's pages and choices are the same, and saves load as they are. Two descriptions are reworded: the SL Aroused options now say they are for SLO Aroused (SexLabAroused.esm) and work with OStim or SexLab. Replace every file: the plugin and the scripts are checked against each other at load, and a mix from two versions stops with a message.

name: v4.2.0 - Colours and Clarity
body:
Magelight UI 0.31.2 is bundled (`98 Magelight UI`):

- Page shapes are anti-aliased again: icons, curves and the quick wheel's slices have smooth edges. `"msaa"` in `Magelight.json` sets it (1 off, 2, 4 or 8; 4 by default).
- After a save loads, pages that are not open load one per frame instead of all at once, which smooths the first seconds of play.
- A page's ordinary console output is no longer written to `Magelight.log`; warnings and errors still are, and `"consoleLog": "all"` brings the rest back.
- A second, Windows mouse pointer no longer stays on screen after closing a menu.
- VR: arrow keys, Delete, Insert, Home, End, Page Down, numpad Enter and numpad Divide type into pages; held keys repeat; the numpad types digits with NumLock on.
- `"toggleKey"` in `Magelight.json` takes a key name ("F3", "PageDown") as well as a scancode, and the log warns about a number that is not a scancode.

Five colour themes for every SeverActions page, popup and the quick wheel, picked in Settings > UI Display: The Ledger (today's look, the default), Windhelm Slate, Dwemer Verdigris, Soul Cairn and Jarl's Vellum, a light theme. With Magelight 0.31.1 or later the cursor takes the theme's colours too. Status, hold, school and money colours keep their meaning in every theme. The Enterprises popup for hiring or managing a retainer follows the theme too, with a new layout: the people to choose from beside the terms, occupation tiles, and a line at the bottom that sums up the hire.

Slot presets stay on after fast travel, sleep and waiting. SeverActions re-applied a preset when a follower loaded and never looked again, so a re-dress by the game or the follower's own mod went unnoticed, and nothing re-checked after a sleep or a wait. It now re-checks a few seconds after every load, sleep or wait, one follower per frame, and re-applies only when another outfit has been put on or a preset piece is missing. A follower's sleep outfit no longer dresses them over a preset either. Situation outfits also switch again right after you close the menu: after editing someone on the Outfits page, their outfit changes stayed paused for up to five minutes.

A follower's inventory shows the armour they carry again. The page hid every item that matched the follower's default outfit, so a piece you freed from it, or a plain copy you gave them, stayed hidden; it now hides only the game's own outfit copies, a note says how many, and a worn one can be taken off with the new Take off button on the character sheet. Giving, selling, dropping and destroying never take an outfit copy. The warmth meter now reads 100% for a full set of warm gear, so ordinary armour no longer shows as "Bare".

Turning off a spell on the Spells page now really stops a follower casting it. A spell from the NPC's own record (a mage follower's Flames) used to stay known while the page showed it off; it is now removed from the record, and turning it back on restores it. Spells from a record other NPCs share, or from a template, cannot be removed for one NPC alone: the page shows their toggle dimmed and says why. Innate spells carry an "Innate" badge.

The quick wheel holds up to twelve slots and draws only the ones you fill, evenly spaced, with every name kept inside its slice.

The Work row on the Companions page places a plain work mark again with Enterprises installed, like Home and Relax, instead of hiring the NPC as your retainer: an NPC can now work for someone else and still keep a routine. Hiring stays on the Enterprises board, which lists a work mark with no terms.

Retainer work stories can be muted: one retainer, a whole hold or a sworn camp on the Enterprises page, or every retainer in a job or on certain terms in Settings > AI. Their gold and goods still settle. Retainers who are dead, captive or gone no longer use up a story at all. Off-screen events no longer write diary entries that put you in the scene, and Settings > Off-Screen Events can turn those diary entries off.

Settings > Hotkeys: a key capture always ends (after a key, Esc, a refusal or ten seconds), clearing a key redraws its row, and in VR the page says keyboard capture is not available there and warns when the menu chord clashes with another binding.

The Life Tracker no longer marks every letter read the moment it opens: only the letter shown at the top is read, and in the Unread view the letters you read stay listed until you change the filter. The World page's first open no longer freezes the game for most of a second, and travel to a named place no longer hitches on the same lookup.

The interface reads more plainly: the over-written wording across the Dashboard, the Actions page, Survival, Enterprises, the Life Tracker, World and the help text says what each thing is, while The Hearth Ledger and Writ & Command keep their names. The hotkey names on Settings > Hotkeys are translated. The Russian translation is corrected throughout, with one word per term (спутник, униформа, управитель, подручный, задание), names no longer forced into the wrong case, and the same hotkey names in the menu and the MCM.

The installer no longer depends on how a FOMOD installer reads an unset choice: the module scripts now always install, so installs made with FOMOD Plus that came out missing scripts get all of them.

Installing this version: install it over 4.1.x with Replace. The installer's pages and choices are the same, and saves load as they are.

name: v4.1.0 - Quicker Commands
body:
Magelight UI 0.30.5 is bundled (`98 Magelight UI`):

- With DLSS or frame generation behind NVIDIA Streamline (Community Shaders' and Open Shaders' upscalers among them), SeverActions' menus no longer open invisible: they are drawn in the game's own interface pass.
- With Community Shaders' frame generation, the menus show again: Magelight no longer writes past the end of that swapchain's function table, which turned its renderer off at startup.
- With NVIDIA Smooth Motion, opening the menu no longer freezes the game: Magelight draws with the game's own graphics device there.
- If the graphics device is lost, Magelight turns itself off instead of leaving the game paused under a menu that cannot draw.
- A new mouse cursor, drawn sharp at any resolution, and only one of it: the game's own menu cursor no longer shows under or over the page.

When Magelight UI cannot draw at all, the menu key and the quick wheel key now say so on screen and point to `Magelight.log`, instead of doing nothing. A menu or popup that could not take focus no longer leaves the game half in menu mode, with other mods' hotkeys muted, until the next time a menu opened.

Wait and Follow answer at the first press. Each command used to undo everything SeverActions could have put on a follower, whether it was there or not: about forty steps that each wait for the next frame, for every follower, every time. It now checks once what is actually there and undoes only that, so a custom follower SeverActions only tracks takes about ten steps instead of forty, and Wait All and Follow All over a full party finish in a second or two. The Companions page updates when the command has finished instead of half a second after the click, when it still showed the old state. A custom follower told to wait is no longer let go for a moment in the middle of the command, which gave their own mod time to make them follow again.

Loading is faster. On a long-running save, SeverActions' start-up after a load took about a minute and now takes about twelve seconds, and a follow or wait command given right after a load no longer waits behind it for twenty seconds or more. Most of the time went on walking pools of hundreds of empty slots one by one; those walks now visit only the filled ones. The load logs also report how long each step of SeverActions' start-up took.

Companions in the follow pool are no longer pushed back onto their follow package every few seconds. The check that notices a companion drifting off their follow package did not know the pool's own copies of those packages, so it read every companion seated there as drifted and re-applied the package five times every five seconds, then every five minutes, all session.

The quick wheel and the menu key work again when bound to a mouse or gamepad button (M3, M4 or M5, for example), as they did before 4.0. Settings > Hotkeys can now capture the mouse's extra buttons, and names mouse and gamepad buttons instead of showing "Key 259".

In Tracking mode, casual follow works again for an NPC no follower framework leads: they follow, wait and resume as in SeverActions mode. Recruiting someone who was casually following you hands them over to their framework cleanly. The Companions page now shows the framework mode the game is actually using; it read an older copy of the setting, which could disagree. With Debug mode on, a notice names each follower SeverActions stops leading after a load because Tracking mode is on.

The Outfits page's live mirror, on Magelight's CPU renderer, starts the Live Stage on its own and shows the NPC there instead of an empty hole through the menu. In VR it shows a dark box with a short hint instead of whatever was behind the panel.

Installing this version: install it over 4.0.x with Replace. The installer's pages and choices are the same, and saves load as they are.

Requires SkyrimNet 0.25 (beta 25) or newer. The full history is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

name: v4.0.2 - Hotfix
v4.0.1 - Hotfix
body:
**4.0.1 Hotfix:** bundles Magelight UI 0.30.2, which fixes:

- a crash at startup or when opening the menu alongside some SKSE mods that hook the game window (the crash log showed USER32 calling an address like `0xFFFF...`);
- SeverActions' menus opening (sound plays, game pauses) but staying invisible with Skyrim Upscaler (frame generation included) or other mods that hook the game's rendering.

Nothing in SeverActions itself changed. Install over 4.0.0 with **Replace**; your 4.0.0 saves load as they are.

name: SeverActions v4.0.0 — Words and Deeds
body:
## **SeverActions v4.0.0** — Words and Deeds

4.0 moves SeverActions onto SkyrimNet 0.25 and a new in-game menu that also works in VR, and NPCs now act on what they agree to, not on talk about later. It adds portraits, a home base for your company in Sever's Hearth, real leashes for captives and steadier routines for the NPCs you house, and fixes a save-load crash, several freezes and many outfit, captive, arrest and camp bugs.

:warning: **Before you update**

- **SkyrimNet 0.25 or newer** - On an older SkyrimNet, none of SeverActions' actions, prompts or triggers load.
- **Magelight UI is included** - It draws the menu, popups and quick wheel, so PrismaUI and UIExtensions are no longer needed (keep PrismaUI if another mod uses it). If you also run Magelight UI as its own mod, let the newer copy win.
- **Visual C++ runtime** - If the menu won't open, install or repair the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable 2015-2022 (x64).
- **Replace, don't merge** - The zip is laid out differently, so replace the old mod (in MO2, choose Replace). Installing by hand? The manual install notes at the root of the zip list the old files to delete.
- **Saves carry over** - Existing saves keep loading, and NPCs mid-journey or waiting somewhere carry on.
- **Renamed actions** - CompanionWait and CompanionFollow are now WaitForPlayerHere and ResumeFollowing: set any SkyrimNet settings you gave them again. An action you edited in SkyrimNet's action editor keeps its old text, so delete your copy and redo the edit.

:speech_balloon: **Actions and the AI**

- **Fewer accidental actions** - NPCs act on what they agree to, are told to do or decide to do right now. Plans, maybes, jokes and threats about later ("we could go to Whiterun some time") stay words.
- **Action categories** - Every action now sits in a category the AI opens first, which gives it a second look and a way to back out.
- **Offered to the right people** - Camping actions go only to your followers, arrest verdicts only to guards, and the jarl's tax actions only while hold taxes are on. Guards no longer arrest you on their own when you have no bounty in their hold.
- **Free seats only** - NPCs are no longer sent to a chair, bench or bed someone else is using, and pick the nearest free one if theirs is taken.
- **Outfit presets by name** - NPCs know the names of their saved presets, so the AI asks for the right one.
- **Property gifts** - You confirm before the deed to a house or business changes hands.
- **Fixes** - NPCs announcing a give, trade or craft to another NPC wait for the answer and back off if talked out of it. Failed magic lessons go wrong visibly, wards are no longer recast until magicka runs out, and the action history no longer repeats or invents what happened.

:art: **Portraits and Bio Blocks**

- **Portraits** - Press Add portrait on the Companions page, pick any picture with the menu's own file browser and frame it with Adjust. Retainers, NPCs you gave a home and your own character (on the Dashboard) can have one too.
- **Shown everywhere** - Portraits appear wherever SeverActions lists an NPC: Enterprises, Outfits, Inventory, Actions, the Life Tracker, the Dashboard, Arrests and the wanted list.
- **Live status** - Each companion's sheet shows their health, stamina and magicka, what they're doing and where.
- **Bio Blocks** - Redesigned for large libraries: categories, a searchable card grid, and Apply to… for several people or whole factions at once. Apply from Library on the Companions page lets you tick a character's blocks and save once.
- **Blocks from other mods** - Other mods can add read-only blocks to your library; Duplicate as my own makes an editable copy.

:computer: **Menu, Quick Wheel and Catalog**

- **New menu engine** - The menu, popups and quick wheel run on Magelight UI, bundled with the pack.
- **Your quick wheel** - Choose its eight slots in Settings → Interface → Hotkeys.
- **Catalog inspector** - Click an item to turn it in 3D and see its stats, effects, source mod and a Give button. Columns sort when clicked, and armor and weapons list by name.
- **Gifts get noticed** - Gear you hand over through the Inventory page or the Catalog counts as a real gift NPCs can react to.
- **Hotkeys** - They work right after a load, your menu and wheel keys stay as you set them, Last Talked To finds the right NPC, and MCM settings no longer reset at launch.
- **Fixes** - A popup choice no longer carries over to a reopened popup, closing with Escape after the wardrobe restores the outfit lock, and Russian counts use the right word form.

:busts_in_silhouette: **Companions**

- **They sit with you** - Sit on a chair, bench or throne and the companions following you take the nearest free seats, then stand when you do (Settings → Followers → Behavior).
- **No more friendly-fire fights** - A Shout, spell or stray arrow from you or a companion no longer turns a follower on you. This covers followers from any framework, a mustered war band and retainers on guard duty.
- **Walk With Me support** - Walk With Me can lead SeverActions companions in its party without SeverActions fighting it.
- **Steadier relationships** - Bonds no longer spiral into devotion or contempt: the assessment resists extremes, keeps to its limits and now also hears voice and vanilla dialogue.
- **Tracking mode** - SeverActions registers every teammate and leads nobody; recruit through dialogue or your framework. Relationships, off-screen life, outfit locks and homes still apply.
- **Fixes** - Followers told to wait indoors stay there, larger groups follow you through load doors, dismissed followers keep their outfit lock, essential status and combat style, and banter no longer goes quiet for good.

:house: **NPC Homes**

- **Routines that hold** - NPCs you give a home, workplace or relax spot keep to their routine more reliably, even when another mod gives them a routine of its own. SexLab and OStim scenes, crafting and spell casting still come first.
- **See what they're doing** - Each card under Companions → Assigned NPCs shows where the NPC is now and which part of their routine they're on (home, work, relax, waiting, with you), or why it isn't running.
- **Relax without a home** - A relax spot now works on its own.
- **Wait means wait** - In Tracking mode, Wait on an NPC nobody else leads keeps them where they are instead of letting them wander off. In SeverActions mode, the Wait hotkey no longer turns a housed NPC into a follower.
- **Property** - Residents of a building you're given now share ownership with you, and older saves where they were left as trespassers repair themselves on the next load or visit.
- **Fixes** - Home, work and relax spots survive a save and load while the NPC is far away.

:tent: **Sever's Hearth and Survival**

- **A base for your company** - The first camp you pitch becomes your base: it stays standing, holds the stash chest, restores the needs of those living there, and followers can be sent to stay. Move it, strike it, or let companions manage it in conversation.
- **Base upgrades** - From a starting camp for two, to an encampment for four, to a command camp with a war tent and a smithy for six.
- **Camps that look the part** - Laid out like the vanilla Legion and Stormcloak camps, with real tents, furniture you can use and nothing clipping.
- **Small camp** - For you and one or two companions, even indoors in caves and dungeons. It never becomes the base.
- **Survival page** - A card per companion with portrait, need bars, Feed and a new Shares food / Own food choice.
- **Fixes** - Followers sent to camp settle in, and turning survival off really freezes needs.

:chains: **Captives and Arrests**

- **Real leashes** - With Leash Framework (and FSMP for rope physics), captives being led, marched, escorted to jail or tied to furniture wear a real tether that pulls them along. 1.1.1 or newer ties it to their wrists; the Leash Attachment setting picks wrists or neck.
- **Restrain** - Binds their hands and keeps them at the restrainer's heel, and can pick up a captive who is already held.
- **Tie to furniture** - Tie a captive to a chair, post or altar yourself, or tell whoever leads them to.
- **Bound means bound** - Captives can't craft, trade, travel, hand over items, change clothes, fight or run a business, but can still talk and plead.
- **Arrests** - Prisoners stay bound all the way to jail, jarls order arrests instead of making them, and searches turn up evidence that fits the charge.
- **Fixes** - Guards no longer get locked in with their prisoner, captives stay bound through load doors, and saves with many tracked bounties load them correctly.

:crossed_swords: **Combat, Brawls and Outlaw Camps**

- **Fight cooldowns use real time** - The cooldown after a brawl, ceasefire or yield now lasts as long as it should; at the default timescale it used to end within seconds.
- **Brawls clean up after themselves** - A brawl, or a save made during one, no longer leaves an NPC permanently aggressive or unkillable, and a fist fight broken up by a weapon or spell simply ends.
- **Loot hint** - The hint that invites NPCs to loot after a fight is now optional (Settings → Prompt Filters → Combat Context), and by default it is only given when a companion is nearby.
- **Sworn camps** - They no longer repopulate, a mustered war band keeps following you after a load, and a sworn member only turns on you after real damage from you.
- **Ceasefires** - They hold and break as one group.
- **Fixes** - Forced fights clean up when they end, a companion who attacks you leaves your service first, and truce settings no longer turn themselves back on.

:moneybag: **Enterprises and the Imperial Levy**

- **The Levy moves to Solitude** - The General and his Legates now hold court at the Blue Palace, and the four-soldier squad patrols Solitude. In existing saves they move once, out of sight.
- **Levy bios restored** - The fifteen Levy characters have their backgrounds again; SkyrimNet 0.25 had stopped reading them.
- **Loans** - A default costs a little renown instead of sending thugs, and a loan is no longer collected twice.
- **Deserters** - They lead the thugs they hired, can be talked down, and can be hired back.
- **Long lists** - Search, filters and folding sections across the Enterprises tabs.
- **Fixes** - Stewards describe their 15% cut correctly, turning the Levy off sends the whole detail home, and jarls and guild leaders no longer write asking to be hired.

:brain: **Character Context and Background AI**

- **Off-screen life** - Now shows for dismissed and home-stationed companions too. The stories know who travels with you, and a jailed companion's life happens in the cell.
- **They know you** - Spouses, employees, stewards and NPCs you gave a home no longer treat you as a stranger.
- **Recovers on its own** - Banter, follower opinions, ambient actions and reputation notes pick up again within minutes if an AI reply goes missing.
- **Cleaner prompts** - NPCs use your name, your inventory isn't pasted into every prompt, and SkyrimNet's log no longer fills with SexLab warnings when you don't use it.
- **Fixes** - The intimacy layer never applies to children, NPCs in quest scenes are left out of ambient banter, background replies no longer land in another save, and dead NPCs are left out of stories.

:dress: **Outfits**

- **Off switch** - Settings → Followers → Outfit System now turns the whole system off, outfit actions and auto-switching included. Presets and locks are kept for when you turn it back on.
- **Your gear stays yours** - Presets, locks and "put on" requests use your enchanted, tempered or renamed piece, never a plain copy, and cleanup never destroys a piece you made.
- **One piece at a time** - "Take off your helmet" now changes only the helmet.
- **Equip sets the outfit** - The wardrobe's Equip button saves what you equip as the NPC's outfit, so their old preset no longer comes back.
- **Live Stage** - The wardrobe can show the NPC themselves in the preview; drag to orbit and scroll to zoom (not in VR).
- **Protected items** - Excluded NPCs are left fully alone, bondage-mod restraints are never stripped or saved into a preset, and other mods' outfit chests (Daegon's, for one) are no longer deleted.
- **Fixes** - Auto-switching no longer leaves spare armor in the pack, multi-word preset names work, situation outfits wait for scenes and undressing to finish, default outfits come back properly, and the preview no longer stretches, mislights or eats video memory.

:compass: **Travel and Stability**

- **No journey limit** - The five-journey cap is gone, and the MCM Travel page lists journeys under way so you can cancel one.
- **Trades, debts and crafting** - Trade offers no longer mix up, payments and debts are confirmed in conversation, and NPCs sent to a distant forge no longer give up after 15 seconds.
- **Stability** - A save-load crash tied to the relationship assessment is fixed, and a notification containing "{0}" no longer freezes the game.
- **Compatibility** - Fertility Mode tracking no longer stalls after a relaunch, and a missing or mismatched native plugin now warns you at load.

:goggles: **Skyrim VR**

- **The menu in your headset** - Point with the controller and pull the trigger. Grip + B/Y opens the menu, Grip + A/X the quick wheel.
- **Freezes fixed** - Loading a long-running save first thing no longer hangs the game, and the RaceMenu VR outfit freezes are gone.
- **Without powerofthree's Tweaks** - Commissions, debts, prison pleas and scene checks now work on VR.

:wastebasket: **Removed or Renamed on Purpose**

- **WaitForPlayerHere / ResumeFollowing** - The new names for CompanionWait and CompanionFollow. Set any SkyrimNet settings you gave them again; every other action keeps its name and settings.
- **StopUsingFurniture** - NPCs get up by themselves when you walk away, and the Stand Up hotkey stays. Delete any copy you saved in SkyrimNet's action editor.
- **SetCombatStyle, SetFollowDistance** - Now on the Companions page or MCM, and the Actions page.
- **LeashCaptive, UnleashCaptive** - Replaced by RestrainNPC, ReleaseCaptive and TieCaptiveToFurniture.
- **AdjustRelationship** - It shipped disabled; the relationship assessment replaced it.

Download: https://github.com/Severause/SeverActions/releases/tag/v4.0.0
Full notes: https://github.com/Severause/SeverActions/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

name: SeverActions v3.9.14 — SkyrimNet Beta 25 build
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This build is for SkyrimNet Beta 25 only.** SkyrimNet Beta 25 loads mod content from per-mod layers, so this zip installs SeverActions' actions, prompts and triggers under `SKSE/Plugins/SkyrimNet/external/severause.severactions/`.
>
> **Still on an earlier SkyrimNet?** Use [v3.9.14](https://github.com/Severause/SeverActions/releases/tag/v3.9.14) instead. On older SkyrimNet builds this zip's actions, prompts and triggers will not load.

**What differs from v3.9.14** (features are otherwise the same):
- SkyrimNet content moved into the Beta 25 content layer (see above).
- `SeverActionsNative.dll` finds SeverActions' prompts and the Final Audit actions in the new location.
- The Abort Pregnancy trigger is now named `abort_pregnancy`.
- **Set Combat Style** and **Set Follow Distance** are disabled by default.

**Installing:** replace your existing SeverActions install (in MO2, choose **Replace** rather than Merge, or remove the old mod first) so the old v3.9.14 SkyrimNet files don't linger.

---

## **SeverActions v3.9.14** — Coming and Going (SkyrimNet Beta 25 build)

:scroll: **Companions**

- **Dismiss / Re-Recruit** - Fixed homed followers not going home (or getting stuck under SA's home sandbox and refusing to follow again) when dismissed or re-recruited through their own dialogue. Covers both NFF followers and custom-AI followers like Sofia and Inigo, who mark dismissals with their own faction and were never noticed.
- **Wait In Place** - New toggle (Settings → Followers → Sandboxing, and the MCM). A waiting follower stands exactly where you left them instead of milling about the room. Off by default; the wide relax remains the behaviour when it's off.
- **NFF Decoupling** - With NFF installed and Recruitment Mode set to SeverActions, followers you recruit through SA are driven by SA directly and never handed to NFF, so removing someone from NFF's menu no longer also drops them from SA. Followers recruited through NFF's own dialogue stay NFF's, as before.
- **Essential** - Followers are no longer made essential automatically. Turn it on per follower from the Companions page; existing essential followers keep it, and the choice now survives dismiss and reload.

:moneybag: **Enterprises**

- **Imperial Levy** - New toggle (Settings → Enterprises / MCM) to disable the Levy entirely while their story is on hold. Turning it off also stands down and removes a detail already in the field.
- **Guard / Attend Targets** - Your own retainers can now be picked as guard or attend targets (they were filtered out of the picker). Both pickers gained a re-scan button.
- **Steward Visits** - Stewards away on a visit now show on the travel map for the whole trip, including the stay at the retainer's side. The Holds pane gained a **Recall** button to send one home mid-journey or mid-visit, and Settings → Enterprises has a new Steward Visit Frequency slider (0 = stewards stay at their posts).
- **Captive Deaths** - A captive's death is now narrated by what actually happened: an execution names the killer (player or follower), neglect reads as neglect. Followers no longer scold themselves for a deed they chose to do.

:pen_fountain: **Bio Blocks**

- **Faction Rules** - A block granted to a whole faction now shows on the block's card chip (e.g. "3 applied · 2 factions") and in the Applied tab, with remove buttons in both places. Search covers faction names too.

:wrench: **Misc**

- **Performance** - Possible performance improvements on the UI front: the hidden menu view no longer redraws every frame from game load, and the Enterprises page no longer keeps polling while the menu is closed.
- **Settings Layout** - Sandboxing controls (Auto-Sandbox at Home, Wait In Place, Multi-Floor Sandboxing, Sleep at Night) now live in their own Followers → Sandboxing section instead of being scattered through Behavior.
- **Outfit Logging** - The "non-preset armor" tripwire now names the exact item, whether it's worn, and whether it came from the NPC's default outfit, so the wrong-armor-after-preset reports can be pinned down from a single log.
